title: NYC subway weekly ridership (MTA daily ridership, data.ny.gov sayj-mze2)
brief: Revision 2, in review: records the owner's decisions of 2026-11-08 (manual weekly download now, subway only, keep the 364-day comparison and flag misaligned holiday weeks) and adds two unscored pilot rounds. Entrants forecast total NYC subway ridership for a Monday-to-Sunday week from MTA's open dataset sayj-mze2 on data.ny.gov. The ranked zero point is one member of a single parameterised year-over-year family, yoy_k(k=4 complete weeks ending D-8, spread rms13), the same rule as the approved Seattle card; on the last 52 weeks it misses by 3.0% against 8.9% for persistence. First scored lock Sun 2027-01-03 23:59 ET (week Jan 4-10), after unscored pilot go/no-go rounds locking 11-29 and 12-06 and three more unscored holiday-week rounds locking 12-13, 12-20 and 12-27. For maintainers: the rights verdict (proposed, not granted) and two person tasks written out in Source: read mta.info/open-data in a browser, and send the question to the publisher.
question: How many subway riders (MTA's 'Subway' mode in dataset sayj-mze2, which includes the Staten Island Railway per the dataset description) will the MTA report in total for the target Monday-to-Sunday week, New York time, as read from SSA's archived resolution capture?

source.publisher: Metropolitan Transportation Authority (dataset owner), published on NY Open Data / OPEN-NY (data.ny.gov), operated by NYS ITS. Dataset contact OpenData@mtahq.org; portal counsel opendata@its.ny.gov [verified, api/views/sayj-mze2.json and the OPEN-NY Terms of Use PDF, fetched 2026-11-09T00:59Z and 01:01Z].
source.access: Route B (owner decision rev 2: manual now; Route A once the publisher or the maintainers clear automated fetching): one person downloads https://data.ny.gov/api/views/sayj-mze2/rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD (the portal's own 'Export > CSV' button) once a week, in the window Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 20:00 America/New_York, and runs an ingest tool modelled on tools/ingest_yougov_xtab.py (proposed name tools/ingest_mta_daily.py). The whole file is about 417 KB and 18,421 rows, so one download carries all history and no query parameters are needed [verified: HTTP 200, 417,544 bytes in 1.0 s, header 'Date,Mode,Count', sha256 af6e2834...eae279, fetched 2026-11-09T00:59:27Z]. Who: the track owner (yhtang@mit.edu) as primary, with a backup named by maintainers at implementation; the card does not name anyone who has not agreed. Saturdays that need covering in the first season include 2026-12-26 and 2027-01-02. What the ingest checks before it writes sources/mta_daily/<capture YYYY-MM-DD>.csv: (1) the header is exactly Date,Mode,Count and every Mode value is one of the nine known codes (AAR, BT, Bus, CBD Entries, CRZ Entries, LIRR, MNR, SIR, Subway); (2) the person passes --downloaded-at (UTC) and it falls inside the Saturday-Sunday window for that week, else it refuses; (3) the newest non-null Subway date is at least the Sunday eight days before the coming lock (D-8), else it refuses with 'Friday posting missing'; (4) capture days are monotonic and a second file for the same capture day must be byte-identical (both rules copied from ingest_yougov_xtab.py); (5) it records url, downloaded_at, sha256, bytes and the newest non-null date per mode in sources/manifest.json via ssa/provenance.py. One download per week serves two rounds: it is the lock capture for the round whose lock is that Sunday, and the resolution capture for the round whose target week ended six days earlier. Route A (automated, only if cleared): the same URL fetched once a day by the scheduled refresh with an honest user agent (as seattle_cad.py uses), never with a token, never in a retry loop (lesson 5). Route A is the same file and the same rules, so switching routes changes no round. Datacenter access is untested from here: a 403 on the first automated day means a local courier (lesson 3). mta.info (the dataset's attribution link) returned 403 to the earlier triage; it was not retried and nothing was done to get around it.
source.archive_policy: Sorted by clause, per docs/sources.md section 9. USE: allowed. OPEN-NY Terms of Use (last modified 2013-03-08), preamble: 'use our government information however you wish' and 'So long as you are not doing anything malicious with NYS data, you may use it as you wish, subject to no other requirements'; Contract: 'You are welcome to freely download and use this Content'; Intellectual Property: 'The State grants you a non-exclusive, revocable license to use the Content' [verified text, data.ny.gov/api/views/77gx-ii52 blob OPEN-NY_20Terms_20of_20Use.pdf, sha256 9437c849...a4cb650, fetched 2026-11-09T01:01:12Z]. MANUAL DOWNLOAD BY A PERSON: allowed, same clauses [verified text]. AUTOMATED RETRIEVAL: unclear. Under the heading 'Public Participation', whose opening sentence scopes it 'To the extent OPEN-NY activates a module or forum for public comment or the uploading of Content or other information from members of the general public', one bullet reads: 'You must not create accounts with OPEN-NY or access the site through unauthorized means, including but not limited to, by using an automated device, script, bot, spider, crawler or scraper.' [verified text]. Against it: the portal's Developers page says 'every dataset on data.ny.gov has an API endpoint' and invites people to 'use it to build your next mash-up' [verified, data.ny.gov/stories/s/2csh-ssf7, fetched 2026-11-09T01:07:36Z], which reads as the API being an authorized means [inferred]. The scope stays open (lesson 10), so the card does not rely on it. REDISTRIBUTION of archived bodies in the public repository: probably allowed [inferred]. The preamble says the terms impose no attribution, share-alike or pre-approval requirement; the IP section bars publishing or distributing Content only 'in a manner inconsistent with the Terms of Use'. The licence is revocable, and the Contract clause says 'Other terms ... may be imposed specifically on specific Content'. MTA's own open-data terms at https://www.mta.info/open-data (the dataset's attributionLink) could not be read: 403 in the earlier triage, not retried [unverified]. The data.gov listing has no licence and the dataset metadata has licenseId null [verified]. Proposed inventory verdict, for maintainers (proposed, not granted): 'approved' for Route B (manual download, archive and publish with attribution 'Metropolitan Transportation Authority, MTA Daily Ridership and Traffic: Beginning 2020 (sayj-mze2), data.ny.gov, captured <date>, unmodified'); Route A 'permission-needed' until a written answer. The agent does not grant either. Person tasks (owner rule G4). Nobody on our side sends or does anything until a maintainer does it or says so. Task 1, for a maintainer: open https://www.mta.info/open-data in an ordinary browser (it returned 403 to the triage fetch; do not script it), and record in this card (a) whether MTA states its own terms for datasets published on data.ny.gov, (b) the exact text of any clause on automated access, archiving or redistribution, and (c) the date read. If MTA terms exist, they decide this card's rights over the OPEN-NY reading above. Task 2, for a maintainer, to send from their own address to OpenData@mtahq.org with copy to opendata@its.ny.gov. Subject: 'Research use of MTA Daily Ridership and Traffic (sayj-mze2)'. Text: 'We run the Social Simulation Arena, a public, non-commercial research benchmark that scores forecasts of public behaviour against official releases. We would like to use the dataset MTA Daily Ridership and Traffic: Beginning 2020 (sayj-mze2). (1) May a scheduled script download the full CSV export (rows.csv?accessType=DOWNLOAD) once a day, with an identifying user agent and no app token? We ask because the OPEN-NY Terms of Use, under Public Participation, bar accessing the site by automated device or script, and we are unsure whether that covers the public dataset export. (2) May we keep each downloaded file unmodified and publish it in our public GitHub repository, attributed to the MTA, as the record our scores are computed from? (3) Do any MTA-specific terms (for example on mta.info/open-data) apply to this dataset beyond the OPEN-NY terms? (4) On which days and at what time of day are new rows normally posted, and are posted counts revised after first posting?' Until the reply arrives, the manual route runs; a written yes to (1) switches the card to Route A in a new revision, and a no to (2) means the archive stays unpublished (inventory 'approved-no-redistribution').

target.population: All subway entries MTA estimates for NYC Transit subway, including the Staten Island Railway (dataset description: 'subways (including the Staten Island Railway)'), as the single published 'Subway' row per day. The SIR row is published separately as well; it is not added, because the description says Subway already includes it [inferred from the description; the overlap is not confirmed numerically, SIR is about 8,000 a weekday against 4.6 million for Subway].
target.window: Monday 00:00 inclusive to the following Monday 00:00 exclusive, New York time, by the dataset's Date column (date of travel).
target.calculation: Sum of the Count column over the seven Date values Monday to Sunday of the target week, Mode = 'Subway', from the resolution capture. Every one of the seven rows must exist with a non-null count; a null row means 'not yet posted' (on 2026-11-09 the rows for 2026-11-04 and 11-05 existed with empty counts) [verified].
target.unit: Riders (MTA estimated subway ridership) per Monday-to-Sunday week. Recent level about 25 to 29 million a week.

lock: Sunday 23:59 America/New_York immediately before the target week (04:59Z Monday in EST, 03:59Z in EDT). There is no publisher calendar; SSA sets and resolves this metric (docs/sources.md section 1.1), as in the approved Seattle card. Schedule (rev 2, owner rule G3: at least two unscored pilot rounds before the first scored lock, because late fill-in has not been measured directly): the ingest tool and the round definitions must be on main by Sun 2026-11-22 (today is 2026-11-08 and a change needs about two weeks). Pilot round P1: lock Sun 2026-11-29, week Mon 11-30 to Sun 12-06, resolution capture Sat 2026-12-12. Pilot round P2: lock Sun 2026-12-06, week 12-07 to 12-13, resolution capture Sat 2026-12-19. Both are posted, locked, hashed and resolved by the full rules, and never scored; this is stated in their round text. Extra unscored rounds (owner decision, 2026-11-08, folded into rev 2): locks Sun 2026-12-13 (week 12-14 to 12-20, capture Sat 12-26), Sun 2026-12-20 (12-21 to 12-27, Christmas week, capture Sat 2027-01-02) and Sun 2026-12-27 (12-28 to 2027-01-03, New Year week, capture Sat 2027-01-09). They run the full rules and are never scored, as their round text says; they add holiday-week pilot data, and Christmas and New Year are flagged because they fall on other weekdays than in the 2025 comparison weeks. First scored lock: Sun 2027-01-03 23:59 ET, week Mon 2027-01-04 to Sun 2027-01-10, resolution capture Sat 2027-01-16; 42 days after the main merge (lesson 7). Its reference weeks (D-35 to D-8, from 2026-11-30) include the Christmas and New Year weeks, compared with 2025 weeks where the holidays fell a day earlier; the round text notes this. If main slips, every date moves a week per week of delay. The doc's own example round (Nov 23-29, lock Sun Nov 22) cannot be run.
baseline: Ranked zero point: one member of a single parameterised family (owner rule G1), yoy_k(start=D-35, end=D-8, whole Monday-to-Sunday weeks only, k=4; spread=rms_n(n=13, search=26 weeks)). With these parameters it is exactly the rule the arena already names 'yoy4' (seattle-community-calls@v4); implementation adds the family once, not a new name per card. Rule: target week starts Monday D, lock Sunday D-1. Reference weeks are the four Monday-to-Sunday weeks starting D-35, D-28, D-21 and D-14. R = (sum of Subway over those 28 days) / (sum over the same 28 days shifted back 364 days), a ratio of sums. Reference mean = R x (Subway total for the week starting D-364). Spread (owner rule G2, measured, never the arena's default sd 1.5): sd = root-mean-square of (actual - reference) over the 13 most recent target weeks complete in the lock capture (W <= D-14), each recomputed by the same rule from that capture; search back at most 26 weeks; fewer than 13 qualifying weeks and the round is not posted. The week D-7 to D-1 is never used: at a Sunday lock its days are not posted [verified, one snapshot: at 2026-11-09T00:59Z, after the last posting of Fri 2026-11-06 23:05Z, the newest non-null Subway day was Tue 2026-11-03, so the week of Nov 2-8 was 2 of 7 days posted]. Measured on the 52 target weeks 2025-11-03 to 2026-10-26 (today's backfill, not first prints) [verified computation, travel-us-scripts/run_mta.py]: yoy4 MAE 745,027 riders, 2.99% of the week (median 2.10%, max 16.0% on the week of 2026-02-23); persistence on the settled week D-14: MAE 2,110,696, 8.89% (median 5.28%, max 46.4% at Christmas). yoy4 beats it in 38 of 52 weeks. Other candidates: one-week YoY (D-14 only) 4.05%; last year's aligned week unscaled 4.03%. Over 200 weeks since 2023-01-02: yoy4 3.63%, persistence 7.28%. R ranged 0.982 to 1.058. Biggest yoy4 misses: 2026-02-23 -16.0% and 2026-01-26 -7.2% (both weeks with a day at about 21-23% of normal ridership, likely winter storms [inferred, cause not checked]), 2026-09-07 -11.9% (Labor Day misaligned; owner decision rev 2 keeps the 364-day shift and flags such weeks), 2026-09-28 +8.9% and 2026-10-05 +7.5% (not explained). Holiday weeks 2025: Thanksgiving week -0.3%, Christmas week +3.3%, New Year week -1.2%. The doc's comparison '3.0% vs 6.0%' is right for yoy4 (3.08% if it could use the unposted week too) but its 6.0% is persistence on the week D-7, which is not posted at the lock; the available persistence is 8.9%. Shown on the board, not ranked: persistence on D-14, spread the same way.
resolution: The weekly capture taken in the window Saturday D+12 00:00 to Sunday D+13 20:00 America/New_York, six days after the target week ends (the same download that serves the next lock). Example: target 2026-12-07 to 12-13, capture Sat 2026-12-19. The resolved value is the target week's Subway sum from that capture. Last year's week and R are not re-read; they were fixed and hashed at lock. Why six days and not the doc's 'Tuesday 12:00': on the evidence the dataset trails by more than the doc says. The Friday 2026-11-06 posting reached only Tuesday 11-03 for Subway (and Sunday 11-01 for CRZ), with Wednesday and Thursday present as null rows [verified, one snapshot], so a Tuesday 12:00 capture would not have the target Sunday. The doc's 'Saturday and Sunday figures typically appear on Monday' (dataset metadata says only 'Data Frequency: Weekdays') is not supported by this snapshot. Rows are posted on business days only: no update between Fri 23:05Z and the fetch on Mon 00:59Z [verified, one weekend], so a Saturday capture equals the data at the Sunday lock. Pilot gate (rev 2, owner rule G3): two unscored rounds, P1 (week 11-30 to 12-06, resolved from the Sat 12-12 capture) and P2 (week 12-07 to 12-13, resolved from the Sat 12-19 capture), plus the late fill-in check they make possible. A maintainer gives the go/no-go verdict on Sat 2026-12-19 after the 12-19 capture is ingested; the holiday-week rounds 12-13, 12-20 and 12-27 are reported with it as extra data, never as the gate. Go if all of: (a) P1 and P2 each resolved from their scheduled capture with all seven Subway days non-null; (b) P1's week total changed by less than 0.5% between the 12-12 capture (+6 days) and the 12-19 capture (+13 days), which is the direct late fill-in measurement; (c) the week of 2026-11-16 to 11-22 also changed by less than 0.5% between the 11-28 and 12-05 captures, a second measurement taken during Thanksgiving week. Then the 2027-01-03 round is scored. No-go: it runs unscored, announced before its lock, and a new card revision moves resolution later (runner-up: Tuesday D+15 12:00 ET) from the measured fill-in.
missing_data_policy: (1) Lock capture missing (no ingest accepted in the Saturday-Sunday window), or any reference day, year-earlier day or last year's aligned day null or absent: the round is cancelled before lock and says so; never posted from an older capture (lesson 13). (2) Resolution capture: if the Saturday download is missed, or any target day is null, a download up to Tuesday D+15 12:00 ET may be ingested instead; if none passes by then, the round is cancelled, never resolved later. (3) Outage check: a target or reference day with a count of 0 or null counts as not posted. There is deliberately no ratio-to-median outage threshold like Seattle's 40%: real storm days fell to 21% (2026-02-23, 830,660) and 23% (2026-01-25) of their 28-day median, so such a threshold would cancel exactly the shocks the track wants [verified computation]. (4) A Mode value never seen before is logged and does not block a Subway round. (5) Backtests above use today's backfill, not first prints, and are labelled that way. (6) Pilot captures that are missed are recorded as failures, not back-filled; a missed P1 or P2 resolution capture is a no-go. (7) Manual-route lapse: two missed Saturdays in a row pause new rounds until a maintainer confirms the rota (lesson 4: a lapsed pull leaves rounds unresolved).
scoring: SSA topline scoring of a predictive distribution over the weekly count, mean and sd (sd > 0) or a quantile map with 0.5, CRPS; arena target_type continuous_normal. Skill = 1 - CRPS(entrant)/CRPS(yoy4). Because last year's week is fixed at lock, scoring the count is scoring the YoY ratio times a known constant, as the doc wants. Check that submitting the reference scores about 0 (lesson 12), 52 target weeks to 2026-10-26: mean CRPS of the reference 582,323 riders; best sd rescaling gains +0.3% (scale 0.85); 90% interval covers 87% of weeks, 50% covers 54%; sd ranged 0.54 to 1.44 million [verified computation]. Over 200 weeks since 2023: +0.4%. With the arena's fixed persistence sd of 1.5 the reference would be a point forecast. Movement (scoring.noise_floor, last 52 weeks): on the weekly count, noise m = 0.92 million, real movement s = 1.85 million; on the YoY ratio, m = 0.031, s = 0.025 [verified computation]. Weekly level changes: median 3.0%, mean 6.1% week to week. Also shown, not ranked: skill vs persistence on D-14, median absolute error, 50%/90% coverage.

assumptions: Rev 2, owner decisions (Claude, delegated by Haoyang Shang, 2026-11-08): fetch route B, manual weekly download now, automated after the publisher or the maintainers clear it; series A, subway only; holiday-misaligned weeks A, keep the 364-day shift and flag the week in the round text. Rules G1-G4 applied: the zero point is named as yoy_k with parameters; its spread is measured (rms13); two unscored pilot rounds precede the first scored lock, which moves from 2026-12-06 to 2027-01-03 (owner decision on the Christmas-week point: unscored rounds 12-13, 12-20 and 12-27 added as holiday pilot data); the two person tasks are written out with exact text.

Dataset and question picked without asking: weekly Subway count, regular tier only. Runner-ups: bus (weaker reference, more weather), CRZ entries (tighter lag, short history), the event-tier joint vector (needs a qualifying shock and the energy score). Reason: the doc's first example and the cleanest series.

Scored as the weekly count, not as a percentage, with last year's week fixed at lock, exactly as the Seattle card. Same CRPS ranking as scoring the YoY ratio; reuses the arena's yoy4 machinery (track/seattle-community-calls-v2, ssa/baselines.ZERO_POINTS) instead of a new target type. Runner-up: a ratio target with its own spread, which needs new arena code.

Resolution six days after the week ends (Saturday capture), not the doc's Tuesday 12:00. Reason: the one snapshot shows Subway trailing a Friday posting by three days. Runner-up: Tuesday D+15 12:00, which is safer but adds three days to every round. Pilot rounds P1 and P2 test the six-day choice.

Manual-route download window Saturday 00:00 to Sunday 20:00 ET, so the capture sits between Friday's last posting and the lock and one download serves both rounds. Runner-up: separate Friday-night and Tuesday downloads.
No ratio outage threshold (Seattle used 40% of the 28-day median); only null or zero counts are outages. Reason: storm days at 21-23% are real behaviour.
Spread rule, 13 weeks RMS, search 26 weeks, copied from seattle-community-calls@v4 rather than re-tuned: here it scores +0.3% for a rescaled reference, close to 0.

Suggested arena names: tracker 'mta_daily'; series 'mta_subway_weekly'; adapter ssa/adapters/mta_daily.py with fetch_text/parse split; tools/ingest_mta_daily.py; archive sources/mta_daily/<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv; round_id 'mta-subway-<week-end YYYY-MM-DD>'. yoy4 currently lives in seattle_cad.py; per rule G1 it becomes the yoy_k family helper at implementation, with this card's parameters (end=D-8, whole weeks, rms13).
